In [[type theory]], a '''polynomial functor''' (or '''container functor''') is a kind of [[endofunctor]] of a [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of types that is intimately related to the concept of [[Inductive type|inductive]] and [[Coinduction|coinductive]] types. Specifically, all [[W type|W-types]] (resp. M-types) are (isomorphic to) [[initial algebra]]s (resp. [[final coalgebra]]s) of such functors.

Polynomial functors have been studied in the more general setting of a [[Topos|pretopos]] with Σ-types;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Moerdijk|first1=Ieke|author-link1=Ieke Moerdijk|last2=Palmgren|first2=Erik|title=Wellfounded trees in categories|journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic|volume=104|issue=1–3|pages=189–218|doi=10.1016/s0168-0072(00)00012-9|year=2000|hdl=2066/129036|hdl-access=free}}</ref> this article deals only with the applications of this concept inside the category of types of a [[Intuitionistic type theory|Martin-Löf style type theory]].

== Definition ==

Let {{var|U}} be a [[Universe (mathematics)|universe]] of types, let {{var|A}} : {{var|U}}, and let {{var|B}} : {{var|A}} → {{var|U}} be a family of types indexed by {{var|A}}. The pair ({{var|A}}, {{var|B}}) is sometimes called a '''signature'''{{sfn|Ahrens|Capriotti|Spadotti|2015|loc=Definition 1}} or a '''container'''.{{sfn|Abbott|Altenkirch|Ghani|2005|p=4}} The '''polynomial functor''' associated to the container ({{var|A}}, {{var|B}}) is defined as follows:{{sfn|Univalent Foundations Program|2013|loc=Equation 5.4.6}}{{sfn|Ahrens|Capriotti|Spadotti|2015|loc=Definition 2}}{{sfn|Awodey|Gambino|Sojakova|2012|p=8}}
:<math>
\begin{align}
  P : U &\longrightarrow U \\
  X &\longmapsto \sum_{a:A} (B(a) \to X)
\end{align}
</math>
Any functor naturally isomorphic to {{var|P}} is called a  '''container functor'''.{{sfn|Abbott|Altenkirch|Ghani|2005|p=10}} The action of {{var|P}} on functions is defined by 
:<math>
\begin{align}
  P : (X\to Y) &\longrightarrow (PX\to PY) \\
  f \qquad &\longmapsto \left((a,g) \mapsto (a,g\circ f)\right)
\end{align}
</math>
Note that this assignment is only truly functorial in extensional type theories (see [[#Properties]]).

== Properties ==

In intensional type theories, such functions are not truly functors, because the universe type is not strictly a category (the field of [[homotopy type theory]] is dedicated to exploring how the universe type behaves more like a [[Higher category theory|higher category]]). However, it is functorial up to propositional equalities, that is, the following identity types are inhabited:
:<math>
\begin{align}
  P(f\circ g) &= Pf\circ Pg \\
  P(\mathsf{id}_X) &= \mathsf{id}_{PX}
\end{align}
</math>
for any functions {{var|f}} and {{var|g}} and any type {{var|X}}, where <math>\mathsf{id}_X</math> is the [[identity function]] on the type {{var|X}}.{{sfn|Awodey|Gambino|Sojakova|2015}}
